discovery: Circuit quantum electrodynamics: strong coupling of single microwave photons to superconducting artificial atoms
subfield: Condensed matter physics / quantum optics with superconducting circuits
motivation: In 2004 Blais, Schoelkopf and co-workers proposed, and Wallraff, Schoelkopf and colleagues demonstrated, that a superconducting qubit coupled to an on-chip microwave resonator reaches the strong-coupling regime of cavity QED, with single photons exchanged coherently between artificial atom and field. Circuit QED transferred the ideas of atomic cavity QED, honoured in 2012, onto engineered solid-state circuits, where coupling strengths far exceed those of real atoms. It opened a new field: photon-number-resolved measurements, microwave quantum optics with propagating photons, ultrastrong coupling, hybrid spin and mechanical systems, and dispersive qubit readout. Above all, circuit QED became the architecture underlying today's superconducting quantum processors and error-correction experiments worldwide. Building on the macroscopic quantum effects recognised in 2025, this work showed how to control and measure light-matter interaction quantum by quantum in electrical circuits, a clean, reproducible discovery that founded a technology.
